description:
crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/proprietary/tantillo2020hcpneutronics.md is partially corrupted by an OCR substitution-cipher artefact. Sections 4 onward render as e.g. 'd n ovr r n :ml:vlmrhou o- r n :.hrh:ml' instead of readable text, and digits are substituted too (1<->6, 2<->7, 3<->9, 0<->2, 5<->J, 8<->@, 4<->F).

CONSEQUENCE: the paper's HTR-10 B1 and B2 result tables CANNOT be read reliably from the markdown, so they were deliberately NOT transcribed into crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/neutronics.rs. Only the passages that survived in plain text were used - the infinite-pebble-bed k_inf comparison (HCP 1.6416, Serpent 1.6321, 0.58% relative), the B1/B2 problem descriptions, the deviated-benchmark deltas, and the isothermal temperature coefficient tables.

ONE FINDING WAS DECODED FROM THE CIPHER AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 7.2: the paper states that large differences have been reported between ENDF/B-VII.0 and ENDF/B-VII.1 results for HTR-10, 'almost exclusively caused by an update in the carbon capture cross section', citing Bostelmann and Strydom (2015). That matters directly - every published HTR-10 value we compare against is ENDF/B-VII.0 (INET's MCNP-4A work is ENDF/B-V), so a calculation on ENDF/B-VIII.0 is not comparing like-for-like. IT SHOULD BE RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE PDF before being relied on.

The PDF itself is fine - crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tantillo2020hcpneutronics.pdf. This is a conversion problem, not a source problem. PROPRIETARY tier (Elsevier): re-ingest for our own use, do not re-host.
title: kovan-literature: re-ingest tantillo2020hcpneutronics - its result tables are OCR-corrupted

notes.content:
DETECTION METHOD, added 2026-08-11. Item (4), the character-corrupted Sod appendix, is caught automatically by the workspace's own mandated README check:

  pandoc -f gfm+tex_math_dollars -t html --mathml <file> > /dev/null

It reports: [WARNING] Could not convert TeX math p / \*ho^\gamma = \text{const}. That is a corrupted \rho.

A full sweep of all 118 git-tracked README.md files on 2026-08-11 with pandoc 3.6.1 produced exactly ONE warning across the whole workspace, and it was this file. Every other README, including the ten that carry LaTeX math, converts cleanly with zero warnings and exit 0. So this is the sole outstanding markdown defect in the repository, which makes it cheap to confirm fixed later — re-run the sweep and expect zero warnings.

CONFIRMING THE BEAD'S OWN WARNING against a fresh look: automated repair really is unsafe. The file contains 160 '*' characters. Legitimate ones are the star-state notation (\rho^*_L, \rho^*_R, pStar) and ordinary markdown emphasis; corrupted ones are single characters substituted at random positions. Observed substitutions include a space in 'rarefaction*relation' and 'a*Riemann', 'i' in 'rarefaction *s' and 'rat*o', 'r' in '\*ho' and '*atio', 's' in 'post-*hock', a backslash in '\sqrt{*gamma', 'n' in 'ha*dy', 'o' in '*f', 'c' in 'post-rarefa*tion', and an underscore in '\rho^**L'. The replaced characters follow no pattern, so there is no rule that separates corruption from notation. Hand restoration against Toro (2013) remains the only safe route.

Only the pandoc-visible math error is machine-detectable; the corrupted PROSE is invisible to every automated check, so a clean pandoc run after a partial fix would NOT mean the appendix is restored.

title: appbuilder: close the Sod / Riemann V&V record gaps (missing numbers, date conflict, corrupted appendix)
